core_obligations: Get a bounded above representative (proof lines 13949-13966): represent the compact object K by a complex and use compactness of K to show that the canonical map to the direct sum of its truncations factors through a finite direct sum, so K is bounded below; then replace the representative by a bounded above complex whose terms are direct sums of elements of S.

Factor the identity through a bounded complex (proof lines 13967-13989): write the complex as the union of its stupid truncations, use the cited results on colimits and countable sums to factor 1 : K -> K through some sigma_{>= n}K -> K, and so obtain a factorisation K -> L -> K in D(A) with L bounded and with terms direct sums of elements of S.

Prove the improvement claim (proof lines 14001-14031): writing L^c as a direct sum of generators, use the first assumption of the statement and compactness of K to cut down to a finite subsum Lambda' through which L^{c-1} -> L^c factors and such that the projection pi composed with varphi vanishes; the kernel (L')^bullet of pi is a subcomplex agreeing with L outside degree c, and the distinguished triangle of the resulting short exact sequence together with homological behaviour of Hom_{D(A)}(K, -) produces a new factorisation through (L')^bullet, so c increases.

Conclude (proof lines 13990-13998): the induction on c yields a factorisation of 1_K through a finite complex L of finite direct sums of elements of S; the resulting idempotent e = varphi composed with psi splits L = Ker(e) direct sum Ker(1 - e), and varphi identifies K with Ker(1 - e), so K is a direct summand of L in D(A).
proof_roadmap: Use compactness to bound the representing complex above.
Replace it by a bounded above complex whose terms are direct sums of generators, and factor the identity through a bounded piece.
Improve the bounded piece degree by degree, cutting down a direct sum to a finite subsum and factoring through the kernel of the projection.
Split the resulting idempotent to exhibit K as a direct summand of a finite complex of finite direct sums of generators.
difficulty_reason: The lemma describes compact objects of D(A) for a Grothendieck abelian category with a generating set S satisfying two conditions: every compact object is a direct summand of a finite complex of finite direct sums of elements of S (statement lines 13933-13946). The proof has three substantial parts: compactness is used twice to replace infinite constructions by finite ones, first to make K bounded below through the canonical truncations (proof lines 13949-13961) and then to factor the identity through a bounded complex L with terms in direct sums of S (proof lines 13967-13989); the technical heart is the improvement claim, where assumption (2) on the functor Hom_A(E, -) and compactness of K cut a direct sum L^c down to a finite subsum through which the differential factors and whose remaining projection becomes zero after composing with varphi (proof lines 14001-14017); finally the kernel of that projection gives a distinguished triangle from which a new factorisation is extracted using the homological behaviour of Hom_{D(A)}(K, -) (proof lines 14018-14031), and the idempotent so obtained is split to display K as a direct summand (proof lines 13990-13998). The claim is H2: a long but completely written-out argument whose only inputs are the two displayed assumptions and standard results of the derived-category chapters.
